**Cases where a chunk boundary matters:**
- **`\r` at the end of a chunk:** it's held until the next character arrives. If that's `\n`, they end the row together. Otherwise the `\r` becomes part of the field, or is a SyntaxError if it comes right after a closing quote. At `end()` it is kept as field text, again with the same error after a closing quote.
- **`"` at the end of a chunk inside a quoted field:** the next chunk decides whether it's a doubled quote or the closing one.
- **BOM:** dropped only if it's the very first character of the whole input, even after empty chunks. A BOM anywhere else is kept as text.
- **When `end()` adds a row:** it doesn't if the input was empty or already ended with a row end, so `"a\n"` gives one row. It does if the last field is empty, so `"a,"` gives `["a", ""]`.
- **Errors:** a quote inside an unquoted field or text after a closing quote throws in `push`. A quoted field still open at the end throws in `end`. The error messages and offsets match `parseCsv`'s, and offsets count from the start of the whole input.

**Tests added to `csv.test.ts`:**

- A timing test: 300,000 small chunks into one quoted field must finish in under 2 seconds. A version whose work grew with earlier input would be far slower.

/**
 * CSV as this service reads it:
 * - Fields are separated by `,`, and a row ends at `\n` or `\r\n`. A `\r` that is not followed by `\n` is part of
 *   its field.
 * - A field that starts with `"` is quoted: it runs to the next `"` that is not doubled, `""` inside it stands for
 *   one `"`, and it may hold `,`, `\r` and `\n`. After its closing quote comes `,`, a row end or the end of the
 *   input, or else it is a SyntaxError. So is a `"` anywhere in a field that is not quoted, and a quoted field
 *   still open at the end of the input.
 * - A `﻿` at the very start of the input is dropped.
 * - The end of the input ends the last row, and a row end just before it does not start another one. An empty
 *   input has no rows; an empty line is a row of one empty field.
 */
export function parseCsv(text: string): string[][] {
  const rows: string[][] = [];
  let i = text.startsWith("﻿") ? 1 : 0;
  if (i >= text.length) return rows;
  const rowEnd = (at: number) => text[at] === "\n" || (text[at] === "\r" && text[at + 1] === "\n");
  let row: string[] = [];
  for (;;) {
    let field = "";
    if (text[i] === '"') {
      i++;
      for (;;) {
        if (i >= text.length) throw new SyntaxError("a quoted field is still open at the end of the input");
        const c = text[i++]!;
        if (c !== '"') field += c;
        else if (text[i] === '"') {
          field += '"';
          i++;
        } else break;
      }
      if (i < text.length && text[i] !== "," && !rowEnd(i)) throw new SyntaxError(`unexpected ${JSON.stringify(text[i])} after a closing quote at offset ${i}`);
    } else {
      while (i < text.length && text[i] !== "," && !rowEnd(i)) {
        if (text[i] === '"') throw new SyntaxError(`a quote in a field that is not quoted, at offset ${i}`);
        field += text[i++];
      }
    }
    row.push(field);
    if (i >= text.length) break;
    if (text[i] === ",") {
      i++;
      continue;
    }
    i += text[i] === "\r" ? 2 : 1;
    rows.push(row);
    row = [];
    if (i >= text.length) return rows;
  }
  rows.push(row);
  return rows;
}

function streamAll(chunks: string[]): string[][] {
  const s = new CsvStream();
  return [...chunks.flatMap((c) => s.push(c)), ...s.end()];
}

test("a stream handles a \\r\\n, a doubled quote and a BOM split across chunks", () => {
  expect(streamAll(["a\r", "\nb"])).toEqual([["a"], ["b"]]);
  expect(streamAll(['"x"', '"y"'])).toEqual([['x"y']]);
  expect(streamAll(['"x"', ",y"])).toEqual([["x", "y"]]);
  expect(streamAll(["", "﻿", "a"])).toEqual([["a"]]);
  expect(streamAll(["a", "﻿"])).toEqual([["a﻿"]]);
});

test("a stream keeps a \\r that is not a row end, and ends rows like parseCsv", () => {
  expect(streamAll(["a\r", "b"])).toEqual([["a\rb"]]);
  expect(streamAll(["\r"])).toEqual([["\r"]]);
  expect(streamAll(["a\r"])).toEqual([["a\r"]]);
  expect(streamAll([])).toEqual([]);
  expect(streamAll(["", "﻿"])).toEqual([]);
  expect(streamAll(["a\n"])).toEqual([["a"]]);
  expect(streamAll(["a,"])).toEqual([["a", ""]]);
  expect(streamAll(["\n", "\n"])).toEqual([[""], [""]]);
});

test("a stream returns a row as soon as its row end arrives", () => {
  const s = new CsvStream();
  expect(s.push('"a\nb"\r')).toEqual([]);
  expect(s.push("\n")).toEqual([["a\nb"]]);
  expect(s.end()).toEqual([]);
});

test("a stream rejects what parseCsv rejects, in push or at the end", () => {
  expect(() => streamAll(['"a"', "b"])).toThrow(SyntaxError);
  expect(() => streamAll(['"a"\r', "b"])).toThrow(SyntaxError);
  expect(() => streamAll(['"a"\r'])).toThrow(SyntaxError);
  expect(() => streamAll(["a", '"'])).toThrow(SyntaxError);
  expect(() => streamAll(["a\r", '"'])).toThrow(SyntaxError);
  expect(() => streamAll(['"a', "b"])).toThrow(SyntaxError);
});

test("a stream equals parseCsv for random inputs and random splits", () => {
  const alphabet = ["a", ",", '"', "\r", "\n", "﻿"];
  let seed = 1;
  const rand = (n: number) => {
    seed = (seed * 1103515245 + 12345) % 2147483648;
    return seed % n;
  };
  for (let t = 0; t < 20000; t++) {
    let text = "";
    for (let n = rand(12); n > 0; n--) text += alphabet[rand(alphabet.length)];
    const chunks: string[] = [];
    for (let i = 0; i <= text.length; ) {
      const len = rand(4);
      chunks.push(text.slice(i, i + len));
      i += len || (rand(2) ? 0 : 1);

export type TextEdit = { old_text: string; new_text: string; replace_all?: boolean };
export type Tier = 'exact' | 'trailing-space' | 'indentation';
// from/to are 1-based line numbers of the replaced text in the original content; count is how many places were replaced.
export type Applied = { from: number; to: number; tier: Tier; count: number };

// Applies one edit to `content`.
//
// Tiers, tried in order; a tier applies only when it finds exactly one place (or replace_all is set, exact tier only):
// 1. exact: old_text appears verbatim. With several matches and no replace_all, it is an error naming the count
//    and the line of the first match. With replace_all every occurrence is replaced.
// 2. trailing-space: compare whole lines of old_text (a single trailing newline on old_text/new_text is ignored)
//    against windows of lines in content, ignoring trailing whitespace on each line. The matched lines are replaced

I fixed `memo.ts` so it does what its doc comment says, and `bun test` now passes: 11 tests, the 4 existing ones and 7 new ones. I didn't run the new tests against the old code, so I haven't seen each one fail before the fix.

**Bugs fixed in `memo.ts`:**
1. **Values coming back after `invalidate`:** when a lookup finished, it wrote its result back for the key without checking that its entry was still the one kept. So a result that was in flight during `invalidate`, `clear()` or an eviction came back. Worse, a late failure from an old lookup could delete the newer one. Both handlers now only act if the entry kept for the key is still theirs.
2. **Memory past `max`:** the size check was `cache.size > opts.max`, so it held `max + 1` keys. It's now a `while (cache.size >= opts.max)` loop that runs before a key is added. Fix 1 also stops evicted lookups from coming back when they finish.
3. **Lookups running too often:** a cache hit didn't move the key to the most-recently-used end, so keys in active use were evicted and looked up again. A hit now moves the key to the end.
4. Two smaller gaps from the doc comment:
   - If `fn` throws instead of returning a rejected promise, the caller now gets a rejected promise and nothing is kept.
   - `size` no longer counts keys whose time-to-live has run out. It clears them out when read, which takes time in proportion to the number of keys.

**Tests:** I couldn't add the tests to `memo.test.ts`: the permission policy blocks changes to that file because the existing tests are protected. They're in a new file, `memo.fixes.test.ts`, with a copy of the test helpers. There's one test for each bug: a late failure from an old lookup, `clear` while a lookup is in flight, a key evicted while in flight, staying at `max`, a hit marking the key recently used, `size` with expired keys, and `fn` throwing directly. If you'd rather keep them in `memo.test.ts`, you can move them there yourself.

2. **Memory past `max`:** the size check was `cache.size > opts.max`, so it held `max + 1` keys. It's now a `while (cache.size >= opts.max)` loop that runs before a key is added. Fix 1 also stops evicted lookups from coming back when they finish.
3. **Lookups running too often:** a cache hit didn't move the key to the most-recently-used end, so keys in active use were evicted and looked up again. A hit now moves the key to the end.
4. Two smaller gaps from the doc comment:
   - If `fn` throws instead of returning a rejected promise, the caller now gets a rejected promise and nothing is kept.
   - `size` no longer counts keys whose time-to-live has run out. It clears them out when read, which takes time in proportion to the number of keys.

**Tests:** I couldn't add the tests to `memo.test.ts`: the permission policy blocks changes to that file because the existing tests are protected. They're in a new file, `memo.fixes.test.ts`, with a copy of the test helpers. There's one test for each bug: a late failure from an old lookup, `clear` while a lookup is in flight, a key evicted while in flight, staying at `max`, a hit marking the key recently used, `size` with expired keys, and `fn` throwing directly. If you'd rather keep them in `memo.test.ts`, you can move them there yourself."}

function deferred<T>() {
  let resolve!: (v: T) => void;
  let reject!: (e: unknown) => void;
  const promise = new Promise<T>((res, rej) => ((resolve = res), (reject = rej)));
  return { promise, resolve, reject };

function lookups() {

    const d = deferred<string>();
    calls.push({ key, d });
    return d.promise;
  };
  return { fn, calls };
}

const tick = () => new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 0));

test("calls in flight for a key share one lookup", async () => {
  const { fn, calls } = lookups();

**Fixes in `runPool`:**
- **Too many tasks at once:** the start loop allowed `running <= limit`, which let one extra task run. It's now `running < limit`.
- **Results in the wrong slots:** results were added in the order tasks finished. Each one now goes into its own task's position (`results[index]`), and the promise resolves once every task has settled.
- **Wrong number of retries:** `attempts < retries` called a task one time too few. A failing task is now called `retries + 1` times in total.
- **Sync throws and plain values (rule 3):** the old code assumed every task returned a promise. A sync throw or plain return broke it. The call is now wrapped in `try` / `Promise.resolve`, so a throw counts as a rejection and a plain value as a fulfilment.
- **Abort (rule 5):**
  - Tasks that never started now settle as rejected with `signal.reason` and `attempts: 0`. Before, they were simply missing, and the pool could hang.
  - A retry is not run after an abort. The task settles as rejected with `signal.reason` and the attempts it made.
  - If the signal is already aborted when you call `runPool`, nothing starts and it resolves straight away.
  - Tasks already running are left to finish and keep their result.
- **Checking `limit` and `retries` (rule 1):** fractions and `NaN` are now refused with a `RangeError`, as well as values that are too small. `Infinity` is still accepted as a limit.

One judgement call: if a task fails on its last allowed attempt and the signal has also aborted, it reports the task's own error, not `signal.reason`, because no retry was being cancelled.

The folder isn't a git repository, so I couldn't review a `git diff`. I checked the final code directly instead.

 * order of `tasks` (not the order they finish in).
 *
 * Rules:
 * 1. `limit` is a whole number of 1 or more, or Infinity; anything else rejects with a RangeError before any
 *    task starts. `retries` (default 0) is a whole number of 0 or more, else a RangeError the same way.
 * 2. Tasks start in input order. A new task starts as soon as one in flight settles, so `limit` are in flight
 *    whenever that many are left to run, and never more.
 * 3. A task that throws synchronously, or returns something that is not a promise, counts the same as one
 *    that rejects or resolves with that value: a throw is a rejection, a plain value is a fulfilment.
 * 4. A rejected task is tried again right away in the same slot, up to `retries` more times. `attempts` is how
 *    many times the task was called in all (1 when it worked the first time).
 * 5. Once `signal` aborts, no task starts and no retry runs. Tasks in flight are left to settle and keep their
 *    result; a task that never started (attempts 0), and a task whose retry was cancelled, settle as rejected with
 *    `signal.reason`, the latter with the attempts it made. If the signal is already aborted at the call,
 *    no task starts.
 * 6. The returned promise resolves once every task has settled; it never rejects except for rule 1.
 */
export async function runPool<T>(tasks: Array<() => Promise<T> | T>, limit: number, opts: PoolOptions = {}): Promise<Settled<T>[]> {
  const retries = opts.retries ?? 0;
  if (!(limit >= 1)) throw new RangeError(`limit must be at least 1, got ${limit}`);
  if (retries < 0) throw new RangeError(`retries must be at least 0, got ${retries}`);

  const results: Settled<T>[] = [];
  let next = 0;
  let running = 0;

  return new Promise((resolve) => {
    if (tasks.length === 0) return resolve(results);

    const launch = () => {
      while (running <= limit && next < tasks.length) {
        if (opts.signal?.aborted) break;
        const index = next++;
        running++;
        attempt(index, 1);
      }
      if (next >= tasks.length && running === 0) resolve(results);
    };

    const attempt = (index: number, attempts: number) => {
      const done = (r: Settled<T>) => {
        results.push(r);
        running--;
        launch();
      };
      (tasks[index]() as Promise<T>).then(
        (value) => done({ status: "fulfilled", value, attempts }),
        (reason) => {
          if (attempts < retries) attempt(index, attempts + 1);
          else done({ status: "rejected", reason, attempts });
        },
      );
    };

    launch();
  });
}

import { expect, test } from "bun:test";
import { runPool } from "./pool";

const later = <T>(ms: number, v: T) => () => new Promise<T>((r) => setTimeout(() => r(v), ms));

test("runs every task and resolves with their values", async () => {
  const out = await runPool([later(5, "a"), later(5, "b")], 2);
  expect(out.map((r) => r.status)).toEqual(["fulfilled", "fulfilled"]);
});

test("an empty list resolves with nothing", async () => {
  expect(await runPool([], 3)).toEqual([]);
});

test("a limit of zero is refused", async () => {
  await expect(runPool([later(1, 1)], 0)).rejects.toBeInstanceOf(RangeError);
});

async function all(text: string, chunk = 7): Promise<SseMessage[]> {
  const out: SseMessage[] = [];
  for await (const m of readSse(streamFromString(text, chunk))) out.push(m);
  return out;
}

test('events and data, at every chunk size', async () => {
  const text = 'event: message_start\ndata: {"a":1}\n\nevent: delta\ndata: {"b":2}\n\n';
  for (const chunk of [1, 2, 3, 5, 64])
    expect(await all(text, chunk)).toEqual([
      { event: 'message_start', data: '{"a":1}' },
      { event: 'delta', data: '{"b":2}' },
    ]);
});

test('CRLF line endings, split between chunks too', async () => {
  for (const chunk of [1, 4, 100]) expect(await all('event: x\r\ndata: 1\r\n\r\ndata: 2\r\n\r\n', chunk)).toEqual([{ event: 'x', data: '1' }, { data: '2' }]);
});

test('multi-line data, comments and unknown fields', async () => {
  expect(await all(': keep-alive\ndata: a\nid: 7\ndata: b\nretry: 100\n\n:\n\n')).toEqual([{ data: 'a\nb' }]);
});

  expect(await all('data:no-space\n\ndata:   two spaces\n\ndata\n\n')).toEqual([{ data: 'no-space' }, { data: '  two spaces' }, { data: '' }]);
});

  expect(await all('event: ping\n\ndata: plain\n\nevent: a\ndata: x\n\ndata: y\n\n')).toEqual([{ data: 'plain' }, { event: 'a', data: 'x' }, { data: 'y' }]);

test('multi-byte characters split across chunks', async () => {
  for (const chunk of [1, 2, 3]) expect(await all('data: สวัสดี 🙂\n\n', chunk)).toEqual([{ data: 'สวัสดี 🙂' }]);
});

test('a body that ends without a blank line still yields its data', async () => {
  expect(await all('data: one\n\ndata: [DONE]')).toEqual([{ data: 'one' }, { data: '[DONE]' }]);

});

test('messages are yielded as they arrive, before the body ends', async () => {
  let release!: () => void;
  const gate = new Promise<void>((r) => (release = r));
  const enc = new TextEncoder();
  let step = 0;
  const body = new ReadableStream<Uint8Array>({
    async pull(c) {
      if (step === 0) c.enqueue(enc.encode('data: first\n\n'));
      else if (step === 1) {

        c.enqueue(enc.encode('data: second\n\n'));
      } else c.close();

  expect((await it.next()).done).toBe(true);
});

`distinctInWindow` is now fast: 200,000 events run in well under a second, where the old version took minutes. `bun test` passes with 10 tests in 65 ms for the whole run.

**What changed in `window.ts`:** the checks and their error messages, the doc comment and the signature are unchanged. I replaced the loop that compared every event with every other one. The new code sorts the event positions by time once, then moves through them in time order. As it goes, it keeps a count of how many events in the current window have each key. Events with the same time are added as one group before their count is read, so they include each other. Earlier events drop out once `t <= t_current - windowMs`. The window boundary is computed exactly as before, so floating-point edge cases come out the same. The counts are written back in the original order of `events`.

**Tests:** I wasn't allowed to edit `window.test.ts`, even to add to it, so the new tests are in a separate file, `window.contract.test.ts`. They cover the parts of the contract I had to preserve:
- events out of order and with equal times count each other
- the window leaves out its start time and includes its end time
- keys are compared exactly, as strings
- a window too small to make a difference when subtracted from a very large time counts nothing (same as the original)
- bad windows (negative, `Infinity`, `NaN`) give a RangeError
- a bad time gives a TypeError naming the index of the first bad event, with the exact message
- 300 random inputs give the same answers as the original definition
- a timing test with 200,000 events and a 1-second limit

**Left open:**
- Arrays with holes in them (sparse arrays) are not handled the same way. The old code crashed on them in a roundabout way; the new code fails differently. I didn't treat them as part of the contract.
- The timing test depends on how fast the machine running it is.

window.ts
export interface Event {
  t: number;
  key: string;
}

/**
 * For each event, the number of distinct keys among all events whose time is in its window: after `t - windowMs`
 * and at or before `t`. "All events" means the whole list, whatever its order: a later entry with the same or
 * an earlier time is in the window too. The result has one count per event, in the order of `events`.
 *
 * `windowMs` must be a finite number above 0, else a RangeError. Every `t` must be a finite number, else a
 * TypeError that names the index of the first bad event. Keys are compared exactly, as strings.
 */
export function distinctInWindow(events: Event[], windowMs: number): number[] {
  if (!(Number.isFinite(windowMs) && windowMs > 0)) throw new RangeError(`windowMs must be a finite number above 0, got ${windowMs}`);
  events.forEach((e, i) => {
    if (typeof e.t !== "number" || !Number.isFinite(e.t)) throw new TypeError(`event ${i} has no finite time: ${e.t}`);
  });
  return events.map((e) => {
    const keys = new Set<string>();
    for (const other of events) if (other.t > e.t - windowMs && other.t <= e.t) keys.add(other.key);
    return keys.size;
  });
}

export type Row = { id: string; [field: string]: unknown };
type Cb<T> = (err: Error | null, value?: T) => void;

let tables = new Map<string, Map<string, Row>>();

export function reset(seed: Record<string, Row[]> = {}): void {
  tables = new Map(Object.entries(seed).map(([t, rows]) => [t, new Map(rows.map((r) => [r.id, { ...r }]))]));
}

const table = (name: string) => {
  let t = tables.get(name);
  if (!t) tables.set(name, (t = new Map()));
  return t;
};

const get = (t: string, id: string): Row | undefined => {
  const r = table(t).get(id);
  return r && { ...r };
};
const put = (t: string, row: Row): Row => {
  table(t).set(row.id, { ...row });
  return { ...row };
};
const remove = (t: string, id: string): boolean => table(t).delete(id);
const query = (t: string, where: (r: Row) => boolean): Row[] => [...table(t).values()].filter(where).map((r) => ({ ...r }));

const later = <T>(f: () => T, cb: Cb<T>) =>
  queueMicrotask(() => {
    try {
      cb(null, f());
    } catch (e) {
      cb(e as Error);
    }
  });

export const db = {
  get: (t: string, id: string, cb: Cb<Row | undefined>) => later(() => get(t, id), cb),

import { HttpError } from '../../errors.ts';

// Cancels an open order and puts its units back in stock.
export function cancelOrder(req: { id: string }, done: (err: Error | null, res?: Row) => void): void {
  db.get('orders', req.id, (err, order) => {
    if (err) return done(err);
    if (!order) return done(new HttpError(404, `no order ${req.id}`));
    if (order.status !== 'open') return done(new HttpError(409, `order ${req.id} is ${order.status}`));
    db.get('stock', order.sku as string, (err2, stock) => {
      if (err2) return done(err2);
      const units = ((stock?.units as number | undefined) ?? 0) + (order.quantity as number);
      db.put('stock', { id: order.sku as string, units }, (err3) => {
        if (err3) return done(err3);
        db.put('orders', { ...order, status: 'cancelled' }, done);
      });
    });
  });
}

import { db, type Row } from '../../db.ts';
import { HttpError } from '../../errors.ts';

// Cancels an open order and puts its units back in stock.
export async function cancelOrder(req: { id: string }): Promise<Row> {
  const order = await db.promises.get('orders', req.id);
  if (!order) throw new HttpError(404, `no order ${req.id}`);
  if (order.status !== 'open') throw new HttpError(409, `order ${req.id} is ${order.status}`);
  const stock = await db.promises.get('stock', order.sku as string);
  const units = ((stock?.units as number | undefined) ?? 0) + (order.quantity as number);
  await db.promises.put('stock', { id: order.sku as string, units });
  return db.promises.put('orders', { ...order, status: 'cancelled' });
}

export async function createOrder(req: { id: string; user: string; sku: string; quantity: number }): Promise<Row> {
  if (!Number.isInteger(req.quantity) || req.quantity < 1) throw new HttpError(400, 'quantity must be a positive integer');

  if (!user || user.active === false) throw new HttpError(404, `no user ${req.user}`);

import { db, type Row } from '../../db.ts';

// A user's orders, newest id first, optionally only one status.
export async function listOrders(req: { user: string; status?: string }): Promise<Row[]> {
  const rows = await db.promises.query('orders', (o) => o.user === req.user && (!req.status || o.status === req.status));
  return (rows ?? []).sort((a, b) => b.id.localeCompare(a.id));
}

import { db, type Row } from '../../db.ts';

// Counts per order status and total units ordered, over all orders of active users.
export async function summary(_req: {}): Promise<{ byStatus: Record<string, number>; units: number }> {
  const users = await db.promises.query('users', (u) => u.active !== false);
  const active = new Set((users ?? []).map((u) => u.id));
  const orders = await db.promises.query('orders', (o) => active.has(o.user as string));
  const byStatus: Record<string, number> = {};
  let units = 0;
  for (const o of orders ?? []) {
    byStatus[o.status as string] = (byStatus[o.status as string] ?? 0) + 1;
    units += o.quantity as number;
  }
  return { byStatus, units };
}

# AGENTS.md

Guidance for coding agents working in this repository. `CLAUDE.md` points here.

## What this is

cedia is a personal coding harness written from scratch in TypeScript on Bun. `SPEC.md` holds every settled decision and the stage order; read it before changing scope.

## Commands

- `bun test`: all tests. One file: `bun test test/layers.test.ts`. One test: add `-t "<name>"`.
- `bun run typecheck`: `tsc --noEmit`.
- `bin/cedia -p "<prompt>" [-m <model>] [--output-format text|json|stream-json] [--permission read-only|workspace] [--allow <rule>] [--deny <rule>]`: headless run. Read-only unless `--permission workspace`. `--check <cmd>` declares a check for the done gate. `--sandbox auto|on|off` controls the OS sandbox for bash (Linux needs bubblewrap, socat, ripgrep).
- `bin/cedia lint-session <file.jsonl>...`: check a session log against the trust invariants. `-m faux` with `CEDIA_FAUX_SCRIPT=<steps.json>` runs offline.
- `bun scripts/cache-probe.ts --model <ref> [--turns 20] [--runs 3]`: measure prompt-cache hits on a real model and name every miss.
- `bun evals/run.ts --harness <name> [--model <ref>] [--runs 3] [--jobs 4] [--budget <usd>] [--only <ids>]`: run the eval tasks against a harness; `--estimate --model <ref> [--measured <results.jsonl>]` prices a run first. Binaries come from `CEDIA_EVAL_<NAME>_BIN` or PATH. Results go in `evals/results/`.

## How to work

Work the pstack poteto-mode way:

- Name the data shapes before writing logic.
- Prove it works: every done-criterion has a test or a command that reruns.
- Decide by experiment (prototype or eval) instead of asking when the question can be measured.
- Small commits, each one a unit that can be checked.

## Rules that are easy to get wrong

- `src/core` and `src/protocol` never import from `src/clients`. `test/layers.test.ts` enforces it.
- Model-visible means logged: anything that reaches the model is an event in the session log first.
- Keep the cached prefix byte-identical (see "Cache rules" in `SPEC.md`). Never edit message 0 mid-session.
- Every `tool_use` gets a `tool_result`, including denied and not-started calls.
- API keys only. Never add Claude.ai OAuth, Cursor login, or any request that impersonates another client.
- Never copy code or prompts from `anthropics/claude-code` (no license) or leaked sources, and never port cedia-rs. Adapted Apache-2.0/MIT code needs a `NOTICE` entry.
- e2e tests use the faux provider and must work offline.

## Research

- `research/NOTES.md`: distilled findings with source paths.
- `research/mirror-docs.sh`: re-downloads official docs into `research/docs/` (gitignored). Grep there before searching the web.
</project_instructions>"}

        change('app.py', ['x = f()  # type: ignore', 'except Exception:  pass', 'raise NotImplementedError']),
      ]),
    ).toEqual([
      'suppression src/a.ts',
      'suppression src/a.ts',
      'swallowed-error src/a.ts',
      'type-escape src/a.ts',
      'stub src/a.ts',
      'suppression app.py',
      'swallowed-error app.py',
      'stub app.py',
    ]);
  });

  test('ordinary code is not flagged', () => {
    expect(
      rules([
        change('src/a.ts', ['try { f() } catch (e) { log(e); throw e; }', 'const company = "acme";', 'type Many = string[];', 'it.each(cases)("works", run);']),
        change('notes.md', ['as any reader knows, catch {} is bad']),
      ]),
    ).toEqual([]);
  });
});

test('changesFromPatch reads a -U0 git patch', () => {
  const patch = [
    'diff --git a/src/a.ts b/src/a.ts',
    'index 1..2 100644',
    '--- a/src/a.ts',
    '+++ b/src/a.ts',
    '@@ -1 +1 @@',
    '-old',
    '+new',
    'diff --git a/t.test.ts b/t.test.ts',
    'deleted file mode 100644',
    '--- a/t.test.ts',
    '+++ /dev/null',
    '@@ -1 +0,0 @@',
    "-test('x', () => {})",
  ].join('\n');
  expect(changesFromPatch(patch)).toEqual([
    { path: 'src/a.ts', added: ['new'], removed: ['old'], deleted: false },
    { path: 't.test.ts', added: [], removed: ["test('x', () => {})"], deleted: true },
  ]);
});

describe('in the loop', () => {
  const steps = () => [
    { blocks: [toolUse('c1', 'write', { path: 'a.ts', content: '// @ts-ignore\nexport const x: number = "1";\n' })] },
    { blocks: [text('done')] },
    { blocks: [text('kept it: the type is wrong upstream')] },
  ];

  test('one reminder names the finding; the second claim ends the run with it in the evidence', async () => {
    const cwd = mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), 'cedia-slop-'));
    const log = SessionLog.create();
    const res = await runPrompt({ log, provider: fauxProvider(steps()), model: FAUX_MODEL, tools: CORE_TOOLS, system: 's', cwd, permission: { mode: 'workspace', allow: [], deny: [] } }, 'go');
    expect(res.subtype).toBe('success');
    const reminders = log.events.filter((e) => e.kind === 'reminder');
    expect(reminders).toHaveLength(1);
    expect(reminders[0]!.kind === 'reminder' && reminders[0]!.text).toContain('suppression a.ts: // @ts-ignore');
    expect(res.evidence?.flags).toEqual(['suppression a.ts: // @ts-ignore']);
    expect(lintSession(log.events)).toEqual([]);
  });

  test('with snapshots it reads the real diff, bash included; unlock turns it off', async () => {
    const cwd = mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), 'cedia-slop-'));
    writeFileSync(join(cwd, 'x.test.ts'), "test('a', () => expect(1).toBe(1));\n");
    const home = mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), 'cedia-slophome-'));
    const snapshots = openSnapshots(cwd, join(home, 'snap'))!;
    const script = [{ blocks: [toolUse('c1', 'bash', { command: 'rm x.test.ts' })] }, { blocks: [text('done')] }, { blocks: [text('done')] }];
    const log = SessionLog.create();
    const res = await runPrompt({ log, provider: fauxProvider(script), model: FAUX_MODEL, tools: CORE_TOOLS, system: 's', cwd, snapshots, permission: { mode: 'workspace', allow: [], deny: [] } }, 'go');
    expect(res.evidence?.flags).toEqual(['test-deleted x.test.ts']);

    const off = SessionLog.create();
    const cwd2 = mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), 'cedia-slop-'));
    const quiet = await runPrompt({ log: off, provider: fauxProvider(steps()), model: FAUX_MODEL, tools: CORE_TOOLS, system: 's', cwd: cwd2, permission: { mode: 'workspace', allow: [], deny: [], unlock: ['slop-check'] } }, 'go');
    expect(quiet.subtype).toBe('success');
    expect(off.events.some((e) => e.kind === 'reminder')).toBe(false);
    expect(quiet.evidence?.flags).toBeUndefined();
  });

  test('detected checks remind once but never refuse', async () => {
    const cwd = mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), 'cedia-soft-'));
    const script = [{ blocks: [toolUse('c1', 'write', { path: 'b.txt', content: 'x\n' })] }, { blocks: [text('done')] }, { blocks: [text('done')] }];
    const opts = { model: FAUX_MODEL, tools: CORE_TOOLS, system: 's', cwd, checks: ['bun test'], permission: { mode: 'workspace' as const, allow: [], deny: [] } };
    expect((await runPrompt({ ...opts, log: SessionLog.create(), provider: fauxProvider(script), softChecks: true }, 'go')).subtype).toBe('success');
    expect((await runPrompt({ ...opts, log: SessionLog.create(), provider: fauxProvider(script) }, 'go')).subtype).toBe('error_unverified_claim');
  });
});

test('detectChecks finds the repo test command', () => {
  const dir = (files: Record<string, string>) => {
    const d = mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), 'cedia-detect-'));
    for (const [f, c] of Object.entries(files)) writeFileSync(join(d, f), c);
    return d;
  };
  expect(detectChecks(dir({ 'package.json': '{"scripts":{"test":"vitest run"}}', 'pnpm-lock.yaml': '' }))).toEqual(['pnpm test']);
  expect(detectChecks(dir({ 'package.json': '{"scripts":{"test":"bun test"}}', 'bun.lock': '' }))).toEqual(['bun run test']);
  expect(detectChecks(dir({ 'package.json': '{"scripts":{"test":"echo \\"Error: no test specified\\" && exit 1"}}' }))).toEqual([]);
  expect(detectChecks(dir({ 'Cargo.toml': '' }))).toEqual(['cargo test']);
  expect(detectChecks(dir({ 'go.mod': '' }))).toEqual(['go test ./...']);
  expect(detectChecks(dir({ Makefile: 'build:\n\tcc x.c\ntest:\n\t./run\n' }))).toEqual(['make test']);
  expect(detectChecks(dir({ 'README.md': '' }))).toEqual([]);
});

<change>
Threads: auto handoff, recall, and threads that message each other

Every headless run is a thread of its project (~/.cedia/projects/<slug>/threads/<id>.jsonl, append-only). <project_instructions path="AGENTS.md">
# AGENTS.md

Guidance for coding agents working in this repository. `CLAUDE.md` points here.

## What this is

cedia is a personal coding harness written from scratch in TypeScript on Bun. `SPEC.md` holds every settled decision and the stage order; read it before changing scope.

## Commands

- `bun test`: all tests. One file: `bun test test/layers.test.ts`. One test: add `-t "<name>"`.
- `bun run typecheck`: `tsc --noEmit`.
- `bin/cedia -p "<prompt>" [-m <model>] [--output-format text|json|stream-json] [--permission read-only|workspace] [--allow <rule>] [--deny <rule>]`: headless run. Read-only unless `--permission workspace`. `--check <cmd>` declares a check for the done gate. `--sandbox auto|on|off` controls the OS sandbox for bash (Linux needs bubblewrap, socat, ripgrep). `--fallback <ref|none>` names the model a run continues on when its quota runs out (default `deepseek` → `anthropic/claude-haiku-5-5`). `--plan <ref>` and `--review <ref>` add the plan and review roles (`claude-code[:<model>]` runs them in the user's own Claude Code); `roles` in `~/.cedia/settings.json` sets all three. `CEDIA_CLAUDE_BIN` points tests at a fake `claude`.
- `bin/cedia lint-session <file.jsonl>...`: check a session log against the trust invariants. `-m faux` with `CEDIA_FAUX_SCRIPT=<steps.json>` runs offline.
- `bun scripts/cache-probe.ts --model <ref> [--turns 20] [--runs 3]`: measure prompt-cache hits on a real model and name every miss.
- `bun evals/run.ts --harness <name> [--model <ref>] [--runs 3] [--jobs 4] [--budget <usd>] [--only <ids>]`: run the eval tasks against a harness; `--estimate --model <ref> [--measured <results.jsonl>]` prices a run first. Binaries come from `CEDIA_EVAL_<NAME>_BIN` or PATH. Results go in `evals/results/`.

## How to work

Work the pstack poteto-mode way:

- Name the data shapes before writing logic.
- Prove it works: every done-criterion has a test or a command that reruns.
- Decide by experiment (prototype or eval) instead of asking when the question can be measured.
- Small commits, each one a unit that can be checked.

## Rules that are easy to get wrong

- `src/core` and `src/protocol` never import from `src/clients`. `test/layers.test.ts` enforces it.
- Model-visible means logged: anything that reaches the model is an event in the session log first.
- Keep the cached prefix byte-identical (see "Cache rules" in `SPEC.md`). Never edit message 0 mid-session.
- Every `tool_use` gets a `tool_result`, including denied and not-started calls.
- API keys only. Never add Claude.ai OAuth, Cursor login, or any request that impersonates another client.
- Never copy code or prompts from `anthropics/claude-code` (no license) or leaked sources, and never port cedia-rs. Adapted Apache-2.0/MIT code needs a `NOTICE` entry.
- e2e tests use the faux provider and must work offline.

## Research

- `research/NOTES.md`: distilled findings with source paths.
- `research/mirror-docs.sh`: re-downloads official docs into `research/docs/` (gitignored). Grep there before searching the web.
</project_instructions>"}

# AGENTS.md

Guidance for coding agents working in this repository. `CLAUDE.md` points here.

## What this is

cedia is a personal coding harness written from scratch in TypeScript on Bun. `SPEC.md` holds every settled decision and the stage order; read it before changing scope. `docs/ROADMAP.md` says what comes next.

## Commands

- `bun test`: all tests. One file: `bun test test/layers.test.ts`. One test: add `-t "<name>"`.
- `bun run typecheck`: `tsc --noEmit`.
- `bin/cedia -p "<prompt>" [-m <model>] [--output-format text|json|stream-json] [--permission read-only|workspace] [--allow <rule>] [--deny <rule>]`: headless run. Read-only unless `--permission workspace`. `--check <cmd>` declares a check for the done gate. `--sandbox auto|on|off` controls the OS sandbox for bash (Linux needs bubblewrap, socat, ripgrep). `--fallback <ref|none>` names the model a run continues on when its quota runs out (default `deepseek` → `anthropic/claude-haiku-5-5`). `--plan <ref>` and `--review <ref>` add the plan and review roles (`claude-code[:<model>]` runs them in the user's own Claude Code); `roles` in `~/.cedia/settings.json` sets all three. `CEDIA_CLAUDE_BIN` points tests at a fake `claude`. Every run is a thread of the project: `--thread <id>` goes on with one, `--handoff-at <n|off>` sets when a long session hands off to a new one, `--spawn on|off` and `--swarm <ref>` control sub-threads.
- `bin/cedia threads [list [--all] | show <id> | send <id> <text> | archive <id>]`: the project's threads.
- `bin/cedia lint-session <file.jsonl>...`: check a session log against the trust invariants. `-m faux` with `CEDIA_FAUX_SCRIPT=<steps.json>` runs offline.
- `bun scripts/protocol-schema.ts` regenerates `src/protocol/protocol.schema.json` after a protocol type changes; `bun scripts/session-fixtures.ts` re-records `test/fixtures/sessions/` after the output of a run changes. `test/fixtures.test.ts` fails when either is stale.
- `bun scripts/cache-probe.ts --model <ref> [--turns 20] [--runs 3]`: measure prompt-cache hits on a real model and name every miss.
- `bun evals/run.ts --harness <name> [--model <ref>] [--runs 3] [--jobs 4] [--budget <usd>] [--only <ids>] [--cedia-arg=<flag>]`: run the eval tasks against a harness; `--estimate --model <ref> [--measured <results.jsonl>]` prices a run first. Binaries come from `CEDIA_EVAL_<NAME>_BIN` or PATH. Results go in `evals/results/`.
- `bun evals/gate.ts [--model <ref>] [--estimate] [--update-baseline]`: the regression gate. Runs `evals/gate/suite.json`, prints the expected cost first, compares with `evals/gate/baseline/` and exits 1 when a model got worse. `--compare <results.jsonl>` re-scores a result file for free. Run it before merging a change to a prompt, default, the loop, a tool or the trust layer (`evals/gate/README.md`).

## How to work

Work the pstack poteto-mode way:

- Name the data shapes before writing logic.
- Prove it works: every done-criterion has a test or a command that reruns.
- Decide by experiment (prototype or eval) instead of asking when the question can be measured.
- Small commits, each one a unit that can be checked.

## Rules that are easy to get wrong

- `src/core` and `src/protocol` never import from `src/clients`. `test/layers.test.ts` enforces it.
- Model-visible means logged: anything that reaches the model is an event in the session log first.
- Keep the cached prefix byte-identical (see "Cache rules" in `SPEC.md`). Never edit message 0 mid-session.
- Every `tool_use` gets a `tool_result`, including denied and not-started calls.
- API keys only. Never add Claude.ai OAuth, Cursor login, or any request that impersonates another client.
- Never copy code or prompts from `anthropics/claude-code` (no license) or leaked sources, and never port cedia-rs. Adapted Apache-2.0/MIT code needs a `NOTICE` entry.
- e2e tests use the faux provider and must work offline.

## Research

- `research/NOTES.md`: distilled findings with source paths.
- `research/mirror-docs.sh`: re-downloads official docs into `research/docs/` (gitignored). Grep there before searching the web.

Implement this change:

<change>
Three independent changes to the loop and the headless client. Each has its own tests.

1. Loop: malformed turns end or recover instead of misreporting
A reply with only thinking (or nothing) gets one reminder, then fails the run, instead of letting an earlier turn's text stand as the result. A refusal fails the run. A tool that returns no output or an object for text still gets a string result, and a non-Error throw is named. Calls that share an id run once and get one result, so the log stays paired. An unknown tool's name is cut to 64 characters in its result. Cut-off calls alternating with cut-off replies still stop at the turn limit.

2. Go on in a new session when the provider refuses a session's history
A bad_request or context_length error after the session's first accepted request means the history itself is refused (a thinking signature, a tool call the API cannot read back, a context past the window), and resending fails the same way: a left-alone run stopped there, and --thread resumed into the same refused session. The run now goes on once in a new session on the same model, as quota fallback does (parentSession, inherited changes for the done gate, recall, a logged note), and a resumed thread whose last session was refused starts a new one. The thread records it as why: 'rejected'; regenerate the protocol schema (bun scripts/protocol-schema.ts).

3. Wait for a spent quota when asked, up to a ceiling
--on-quota wait:<minutes> (or onQuota in user settings) waits in the same session for a quota error that says when it comes back (a 429 with retry-after), up to that many minutes across the whole run, and falls back only past it. A spent balance names no time and still falls back at once. The default stays fallback. Each wait is a logged attempt, a stderr line, and ends on SIGTERM.
</change>

<project_instructions path="AGENTS.md">
# AGENTS.md

Guidance for coding agents working in this repository. `CLAUDE.md` points here.

## What this is

cedia is a personal coding harness written from scratch in TypeScript on Bun. `SPEC.md` holds every settled decision and the stage order; read it before changing scope. `docs/ROADMAP.md` says what comes next.

## Commands

- `bun test`: all tests. One file: `bun test test/layers.test.ts`. One test: add `-t "<name>"`.
- `bun run typecheck`: `tsc --noEmit`.
- `bin/cedia -p "<prompt>" [-m <model>] [--output-format text|json|stream-json] [--permission read-only|workspace] [--allow <rule>] [--deny <rule>]`: headless run. Read-only unless `--permission workspace`. `--check <cmd>` declares a check for the done gate. `--sandbox auto|on|off` controls the OS sandbox for bash (Linux needs bubblewrap, socat, ripgrep). `--fallback <ref|none>` names the model a run continues on when its quota runs out (default `deepseek` → `anthropic/claude-haiku-5-5`). `--plan <ref>` and `--review <ref>` add the plan and review roles (`claude-code[:<model>]` runs them in the user's own Claude Code); `roles` in `~/.cedia/settings.json` sets all three. `CEDIA_CLAUDE_BIN` points tests at a fake `claude`. Every run is a thread of the project: `--thread <id>` goes on with one, `--handoff-at <n|off>` sets when a long session hands off to a new one, `--spawn on|off` and `--swarm <ref>` control sub-threads.
- `bin/cedia threads [list [--all] | show <id> | send <id> <text> | archive <id>]`: the project's threads.
- `bin/cedia lint-session <file.jsonl>...`: check a session log against the trust invariants. `-m faux` with `CEDIA_FAUX_SCRIPT=<steps.json>` runs offline.
- `bun scripts/protocol-schema.ts` regenerates `src/protocol/protocol.schema.json` after a protocol type changes; `bun scripts/session-fixtures.ts` re-records `test/fixtures/sessions/` after the output of a run changes. `test/fixtures.test.ts` fails when either is stale.
- `bun scripts/cache-probe.ts --model <ref> [--turns 20] [--runs 3]`: measure prompt-cache hits on a real model and name every miss.
- `bun evals/run.ts --harness <name> [--model <ref>] [--runs 3] [--jobs 4] [--budget <usd>] [--only <ids>] [--cedia-arg=<flag>]`: run the eval tasks against a harness; `--estimate --model <ref> [--measured <results.jsonl>]` prices a run first. Binaries come from `CEDIA_EVAL_<NAME>_BIN` or PATH. Results go in `evals/results/`.
- `bun evals/gate.ts [--model <ref>] [--estimate] [--update-baseline]`: the regression gate. Runs `evals/gate/suite.json`, prints the expected cost first, compares with `evals/gate/baseline/` and exits 1 when a model got worse. `--compare <results.jsonl>` re-scores a result file for free. Run it before merging a change to a prompt, default, the loop, a tool or the trust layer (`evals/gate/README.md`).

## How to work

Work the pstack poteto-mode way:

- Name the data shapes before writing logic.
- Prove it works: every done-criterion has a test or a command that reruns.
- Decide by experiment (prototype or eval) instead of asking when the question can be measured.
- Small commits, each one a unit that can be checked.

## Rules that are easy to get wrong

- `src/core` and `src/protocol` never import from `src/clients`. `test/layers.test.ts` enforces it.
- Model-visible means logged: anything that reaches the model is an event in the session log first.
- Keep the cached prefix byte-identical (see "Cache rules" in `SPEC.md`). Never edit message 0 mid-session.
- Every `tool_use` gets a `tool_result`, including denied and not-started calls.
- API keys only. Never add Claude.ai OAuth, Cursor login, or any request that impersonates another client.
- Never copy code or prompts from `anthropics/claude-code` (no license) or leaked sources, and never port cedia-rs. Adapted Apache-2.0/MIT code needs a `NOTICE` entry.
- e2e tests use the faux provider and must work offline.

## Research

- `research/NOTES.md`: distilled findings with source paths.
- `research/mirror-docs.sh`: re-downloads official docs into `research/docs/` (gitignored). Grep there before searching the web.
</project_instructions>

<change>
Three independent changes to the loop and the headless client. Each has its own tests.

1. Loop: malformed turns end or recover instead of misreporting

A reply with only thinking (or nothing) gets one reminder, then fails the run, instead of letting an earlier turn's text stand as the result. A refusal fails the run. A tool that returns no output or an object for text still gets a string result, and a non-Error throw is named. Calls that share an id run once and get one result, so the log stays paired. An unknown tool's name is cut to 64 characters in its result. Cut-off calls alternating with cut-off replies still stop at the turn limit.

2. Go on in a new session when the provider refuses a session's history

A bad_request or context_length error after the session's first accepted request means the history itself is refused (a thinking signature, a tool call the API cannot read back, a context past the window), and resending fails the same way: a left-alone run stopped there, and --thread resumed into the same refused session. The run now goes on once in a new session on the same model, as quota fallback does (parentSession, inherited changes for the done gate, recall, a logged note), and a resumed thread whose last session was refused starts a new one. The thread records it as why: 'rejected'; regenerate the protocol schema (bun scripts/protocol-schema.ts).

3. Wait for a spent quota when asked, up to a ceiling

--on-quota wait:<minutes> (or onQuota in user settings) waits in the same session for a quota error that says when it comes back (a 429 with retry-after), up to that many minutes across the whole run, and falls back only past it. A spent balance names no time and still falls back at once. The default stays fallback. Each wait is a logged attempt, a stderr line, and ends on SIGTERM.
</change>

The code broke four of the README's pricing rules, and I fixed all four. `bun test` passes: 8 tests, including 4 new ones in `test/rules.test.ts`. I didn't change the existing tests.

**What was wrong and what changed:**
1. **Bulk tiers (rule 2):** `src/pricing/discounts/bulk.ts` checked `quantity > t.min`, so exactly 10 or 50 units got no discount or the lower one. It now uses `>=`.
2. **Merging lines by SKU (rule 2):** `mergeLines` in `src/cart/merge.ts` existed, but nothing called it. So 6 + 4 pens were priced as two lines and missed the 10-unit discount. `totals()` in `src/order/total.ts` now merges lines before pricing them.
3. **Free-shipping threshold (rule 4):** `totals()` compared the threshold against the subtotal before the coupon. It now uses the discounted subtotal.
4. **UK region table:** the UK free-shipping threshold in `src/pricing/regions.ts` was 4500. The README says 4000, so I changed it.

**Checked and found correct:** line subtotals, the coupons (FLAT5 never goes below zero; one coupon per order), tax on the discounted subtotal plus shipping, the total, and the US/EU region entries. I also ran a script over every amount up to 200,000 cents at the 5%, 7%, 10% and 20% rates. The half-up rounding gave the right answer every time, with no floating-point errors.

Each new test covers one fix, with the expected values worked out by hand from the README. I didn't run the new tests against the old code to watch them fail. Also, the folder isn't a git repository, so I couldn't run `git diff` to review the changes.

## Pricing rules

1. A line's subtotal is unit price times quantity.
2. Bulk discount: a line with **10 or more** units gets 5% off that line; **50 or more** units gets 10% off. Only the highest tier applies. Units count per SKU across the whole cart: lines of the same SKU are merged into one before pricing.

6. The total is discounted subtotal + shipping + tax.

//
// slugify(text, max?):
// - lower case;
// - a letter with an accent or other diacritic loses it (à -> a, ç -> c, ñ -> n, ź -> z, and so on);
//   ß -> ss, æ -> ae, œ -> oe, ø -> o, ł -> l, đ -> d;
// - any other character that is not a-z or 0-9 is a separator; runs of separators become one "-", and the slug
//   never starts or ends with "-";
// - with max, a slug longer than max is cut at the last "-" that keeps it within max (no dangling "-"), or at
//   max itself when there is no "-" to cut at. A "-" right after the first max characters counts: cutting there
//   keeps exactly max ("ab-cd-ef" with max 5 is "ab-cd").
//
// uniqueSlug(slug, taken): slug itself if it is not in taken, else slug-2, slug-3, ... the first free one.
const SPECIAL: Record<string, string> = { ß: 'ss', æ: 'ae', œ: 'oe', ø: 'o', ł: 'l', đ: 'd' };

export function slugify(text: string, max?: number): string {
  const slug = text
    .toLowerCase()
    .replace(/[ßæœøłđ]/g, (c) => SPECIAL[c])
    .normalize('NFD')
    .replace(/\p{M}/gu, '')
    .replace(/[^a-z0-9]+/g, '-')
    .replace(/^-|-$/g, '');
  if (max === undefined || slug.length <= max) return slug;
  const cut = slug.slice(0, max + 1).lastIndexOf('-');
  return cut > 0 ? slug.slice(0, cut) : slug.slice(0, max);
}

export function uniqueSlug(slug: string, taken: Set<string>): string {
  if (!taken.has(slug)) return slug;
  for (let n = 2; ; n++) {
    const candidate = `${slug}-${n}`;
    if (!taken.has(candidate)) return candidate;
  }
}

//
// parseDuration: one or more <number><unit> parts, optionally separated by spaces: "90s", "1h30m", "1.5h",

  ['h', 3_600_000],

  ['s', 1_000],

const UNIT_MS = new Map(UNITS);

export function parseDuration(text: string): number {

const SPECIAL: Record<string, string> = { ß: 'ss', æ: 'ae', œ: 'oe', ø: 'o', ł: 'l', đ: 'd' };

export function slugify(text: string, max?: number): string {
  const slug = text
    .toLowerCase()
    .replace(/[ßæœøłđ]/g, (c) => SPECIAL[c])
    .normalize('NFD')
    .replace(/\p{M}/gu, '')
    .replace(/[^a-z0-9]+/g, '-')
    .replace(/^-|-$/g, '');

  const cut = slug.slice(0, max + 1).lastIndexOf('-');
  return cut > 0 ? slug.slice(0, cut) : slug.slice(0, max);
}

export function uniqueSlug(slug: string, taken: Set<string>): string {
  if (!taken.has(slug)) return slug;

    const candidate = `${slug}-${n}`;
    if (!taken.has(candidate)) return candidate;

import { expect, test } from 'bun:test';
import { type EvictReason, LRU } from '../src/lru.ts';

function make(capacity: number) {
  const clock = { t: 0 };
  const cache = new LRU<string, number>(capacity, 1000, () => clock.t);
  const evicted: [string, number, EvictReason][] = [];
  cache.onEvict = (k, v, r) => evicted.push([k, v, r]);
  return { clock, cache, evicted };
}

test('get refreshes recency', () => {
  const { cache, evicted } = make(2);
  cache.set('a', 1);
  cache.set('b', 2);
  expect(cache.get('a')).toBe(1);
  cache.set('c', 3);
  expect(cache.keys()).toEqual(['c', 'a']);
  expect(evicted).toEqual([['b', 2, 'capacity']]);
});

test('set on an existing key refreshes ttl and recency', () => {
  const { clock, cache } = make(2);
  cache.set('a', 1);
  clock.t = 500;
  cache.set('a', 10);
  clock.t = 1200;
  expect(cache.get('a')).toBe(10);
  clock.t = 1500;
  expect(cache.get('a')).toBeUndefined();
});

test('expired entry removed on get', () => {
  const { clock, cache, evicted } = make(2);
  cache.set('a', 1);
  clock.t = 999;
  expect(cache.get('a')).toBe(1);
  clock.t = 1000;
  expect(cache.get('a')).toBeUndefined();
  expect(evicted).toEqual([['a', 1, 'expired']]);
});

test('expired entries are removed before live ones on overflow', () => {
  const { clock, cache, evicted } = make(2);
  cache.set('a', 1);
  clock.t = 500;
  cache.set('b', 2);
  clock.t = 1000;
  cache.set('c', 3);
  expect(evicted).toEqual([['a', 1, 'expired']]);
  expect(cache.keys()).toEqual(['c', 'b']);
});

test('capacity counts expired entries until overflow', () => {
  const { clock, cache, evicted } = make(2);
  cache.set('a', 1);
  clock.t = 1000;
  cache.set('b', 2);
  expect(evicted).toEqual([]);
  expect(cache.size).toBe(1);
});

test('delete', () => {
  const { clock, cache, evicted } = make(3);
  cache.set('a', 1);
  cache.set('b', 2);
  expect(cache.delete('a')).toBe(true);
  expect(cache.delete('a')).toBe(false);
  clock.t = 1000;
  expect(cache.delete('b')).toBe(false);
  expect(evicted).toEqual([
    ['a', 1, 'delete'],
    ['b', 2, 'expired'],
  ]);
  expect(cache.size).toBe(0);
});

test('size and keys count only live entries', () => {

  cache.set('a', 1);
  clock.t = 500;
  cache.set('b', 2);
  expect(cache.size).toBe(2);
  expect(cache.keys()).toEqual(['b', 'a']);
  clock.t = 1000;
  expect(cache.size).toBe(1);
  expect(cache.keys()).toEqual(['b']);
});

import { expect, test } from 'bun:test';
import { type EvictReason, LRU } from '../src/lru.ts';

function make(capacity: number) {
  const clock = { t: 0 };
  const cache = new LRU<string, number>(capacity, 1000, () => clock.t);
  const evicted: [string, number, EvictReason][] = [];
  cache.onEvict = (k, v, r) => evicted.push([k, v, r]);
  return { clock, cache, evicted };
}

test('get refreshes recency', () => {
  const { cache, evicted } = make(2);
  cache.set('a', 1);
  cache.set('b', 2);
  expect(cache.get('a')).toBe(1);
  cache.set('c', 3);
  expect(cache.keys()).toEqual(['c', 'a']);
  expect(evicted).toEqual([['b', 2, 'capacity']]);
});

test('set on an existing key refreshes ttl and recency', () => {
  const { clock, cache } = make(2);
  cache.set('a', 1);
  clock.t = 500;
  cache.set('a', 10);
  clock.t = 1200;
  expect(cache.get('a')).toBe(10);
  clock.t = 1500;
  expect(cache.get('a')).toBeUndefined();
});

test('expired entry removed on get', () => {
  const { clock, cache, evicted } = make(2);
  cache.set('a', 1);
  clock.t = 999;
  expect(cache.get('a')).toBe(1);
  clock.t = 1000;
  expect(cache.get('a')).toBeUndefined();
  expect(evicted).toEqual([['a', 1, 'expired']]);
});

test('expired entries are removed before live ones on overflow', () => {
  const { clock, cache, evicted } = make(2);
  cache.set('a', 1);
  clock.t = 500;
  cache.set('b', 2);
  clock.t = 1000;
  cache.set('c', 3);
  expect(evicted).toEqual([['a', 1, 'expired']]);
  expect(cache.keys()).toEqual(['c', 'b']);
});

test('capacity counts expired entries until overflow', () => {
  const { clock, cache, evicted } = make(2);
  cache.set('a', 1);
  clock.t = 1000;
  cache.set('b', 2);
  expect(evicted).toEqual([]);
  expect(cache.size).toBe(1);
});

test('delete', () => {
  const { clock, cache, evicted } = make(3);
  cache.set('a', 1);
  cache.set('b', 2);
  expect(cache.delete('a')).toBe(true);
  expect(cache.delete('a')).toBe(false);
  clock.t = 1000;
  expect(cache.delete('b')).toBe(false);
  expect(evicted).toEqual([
    ['a', 1, 'delete'],
    ['b', 2, 'expired'],
  ]);
  expect(cache.size).toBe(0);
});

test('size and keys count only live entries', () => {
  const { clock, cache } = make(3);
  cache.set('a', 1);
  clock.t = 500;
  cache.set('b', 2);
  expect(cache.size).toBe(2);
  expect(cache.keys()).toEqual(['b', 'a']);
  clock.t = 1000;
  expect(cache.size).toBe(1);
  expect(cache.keys()).toEqual(['b']);
});
